## Why This Is Asked
This question probes designing scalable, isolated backends while reusing a single module, plus practical CI/CD enforcement and drift-safe promotion.

## Key Concepts
- Multi-tenant backend design with per-tenant keys
- Shared modules with per-tenant variables
- CI plan gating and JSON-based validation
- Drift detection and safe promotion workflow
- Security considerations and least privilege

```terraform
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket         = "tf-state-bucket"
    key            = "tenants/${var.tenant}/prod/terraform.tfstate"
    region         = "us-east-1"
    dynamodb_table = "tf-locks"
    encrypt        = true
  }
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

- Backend aliasing per environment
- terraform_remote_state data

```hcl
# Terraform backend alias (canary)
terraform {
  backend "s3" {

    region = 'us-east-1'
    bucket = 'org-terraform-state'
  }
}
```

```hcl
data "terraform_remote_state" "prod" {
  backend = 's3'
  config = {
    bucket = 'org-terraform-state-prod'

    region = 'us-east-1'

}
```

```hcl
provider "aws" {

  region = 'us-west-2'
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of safe, targeted drift remediation using Terraform's lifecycle and -target, avoiding mass changes.

## Key Concepts

- Lifecycle replace_triggered_by
- Data external sources for dynamic inputs
- Targeted applies with -target to minimize blast radius

## Code Example

```hcl
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "https_prod" {
  type              = "ingress"
  from_port         = 443
  to_port           = 443
  protocol          = "tcp"
  security_group_id = module.network["prod"].aws_security_group.web.id
  cidr_blocks       = data.external.allowlist.result
  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [data.external.allowlist.version]
  }
}

data "external" "allowlist" {
  program = ["bash","scripts/get_allowlist.sh"]
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this in canary before prod rollout?
- How do you handle partial failures if -target changes multiple resources?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests a beginner-friendly CI workflow that ensures per-environment state isolation and safe planning in a PR.

## Key Concepts
- Remote state isolation per environment
- Detecting touched environments from PRs
- Backend config with terraform init -backend-config
- Generating and summarizing plans for PR checks
- Posting results back to PR without affecting untouched envs

## Code Example
```bash
# Pseudo-example
CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only origin/main -- envs/ | awk -F/ '{print $2}' | sort -u)
for ENV in $CHANGED; do
  terraform init -backend-config=key=envs/$ENV/terraform.tfstate -backend-config=bucket=tf-state-bucket
  terraform plan -var-file=envs/$ENV/vars.tfvars -out=tfplan-$ENV
  terraform show -json tfplan-$ENV > plan-$ENV.json
done
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this for parallel plans without race conditions?
- How would you handle secret leakage if vars files contain sensitive data?

## Code Example
```hcl
# modules/iam/main.tf
resource "aws_iam_role" "this" {
  name               = var.name
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.assume.json
}

data "aws_iam_policy_document" "assume" {
  statement {
    effect = "Allow"
    principals {
      type        = "Service"
      identifiers = ["ec2.amazonaws.com"]
    }
    actions = ["sts:AssumeRole"]
  }
}

# modules/bucket/main.tf
resource "aws_s3_bucket" "this" {
  bucket = var.bucket_name
}

# environments/dev/main.tf
module "iam" {
  source = "../../modules/iam"
  name   = "existing-role-name"
}

module "bucket" {
  source      = "../../modules/bucket"
  bucket_name = "existing-bucket-name"
}
```

## Minimal CI Gating Snippet
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Run import and plan
export TF_VAR_name="existing-role-name"
export TF_VAR_bucket_name="existing-bucket-name"

terraform init -backend-config="key=envs/dev/terraform.tfstate"
terraform import module.iam.aws_iam_role.this arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/existing-role
terraform import module.bucket.aws_s3_bucket.this existing-bucket-name

# Verify no drift before allowing apply
terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
if grep -q "No changes" plan.tfplan; then
    echo "Import verified - no drift detected"
    terraform apply plan.tfplan
else
    echo "ERROR: Drift detected after import. Review plan output."
    exit 1
fi
```
